newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 16.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Monday.
- European Union leaders appeared ready to paper over a rift on the single currency last night after finance ministers reported progress on the eve of a contentious EU summit.
- Almost 150,000 Irish people will today enjoy a 250 million share bonanza as a result of Norwich Union's flotation on the London Stock Exchange.
- The final draft of the programme for government between Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats will be presented to both party leaders tonight.
- Cost, high entry charges and the complex nature of pension products have emerged as the main reasons why some people in employment choose not to belong to a pension scheme.
- Europe's single currency project hung on a knife-edge last night as France clung to demands for an easing of the tough economic terms for monetary union.
- The British government launched a fresh initiative to try to resolve the parades crisis in Northern Ireland, three weeks before the marching season gets into full swing.
- A 20 million punt deal is due to be signed this week between Irish transport group CIE and Esat Telecom to set up Ireland's second land-based national telephone network in 12 to 18 months.
